author: jtraglia
content:
* We have not specified additional rewards for aggregators. I do not believe it will be necessary.
* Regarding hardware, the Apple M4 (base, pro, max?) is a very good processor. Very few people run validators on Apple hardware though. A top of the line NUC from 2024 is noticeably worse than even the base M4. I think the typical solo-staker uses a NUC from a few years ago. Have you benchmarked leanVM with one of those?

author: jtraglia
content:
Ah the M4 Max was used. That's quite a beefy machine imo.
> machine: M4 Max MacBook Pro (12 performance cores, 4 efficiency cores, 48GB RAM, CPU only, i.e. no metal GPU)

author: potuz
content: We could always add a special role for aggregators but that is a much larger change

author: potuz
content: I can run benches on my validating node, does the library include standard benches to run?

author: tcoratger
content:
You can find a benchmark page here that includes various machines, including Linux-based ones: https://leanvm.org/. At the bottom of the page, there is a "How to reproduce" section that explains how to run these benchmarks locally.

I have an older M1 MacBook, and in my experience, benchmarks from leanVM on this device were typically 3 to 4 times slower than on an M4. But this is a very old machine and it is super slow for everything in general.

author: potuz
content: benchmarking on ARM or similar architectures, specially for hashing, should be taken with a grain of salt. Most data centers run on Xeons.
